title: MAINE-Seq/Mnase-Seq/Nucleo-Seq
scope: Illumina explanatory family schematic, whose caption co-designates MAINE-Seq and MNase-Seq: nucleosome-associated genomic DNA undergoes MNase digestion, trimmed-complex isolation and DNA extraction. Broad library preparation and deep sequencing are included only as explicit downstream interfaces in the card text; the PNG ends at DNA. The card-associated Nucleo-Seq and contextual Nuc-seq names are matched only to transformations supported by their cited implementations. This is a protection-based DNA architecture, not an assertion that all named protocols share the same isolation order or platform. No retained branch is drawn; FAIRE, ChEC-seq, in-vitro nucleosome controls, RNA-seq and separate methylation datasets in the papers are not depicted routes.

states.label: Open chromatin
features: Genomic DNA associated with gray nucleosome particles; exposed linker DNA connects the particles.
Open chromatin is the depicted starting-state label, not a separately shown chromatin-opening procedure.
The left title illustration repeats chromatin with yellow-highlighted wraps. No arrow connects it to the workflow start, and no legend assigns the yellow a chemical modification.

states.label: MNase-digested chromatin containing protected DNA-protein complexes
features: Exposed/linker DNA is preferentially digested; protein-associated DNA is retained for particle isolation.
The digestion panel still draws connected DNA with orange circles; the next panel shows the resulting separated particles.
Retained DNA is enriched for nuclease protection. Continued digestion can also cleave DNA within nucleosomal particles.

evidence.locator: Arrow from Open chromatin to MNase digestion; orange circles alongside the DNA

evidence.quote: In MNase-Seq, gDNA is treated with MNase. Sequences bound by chromatin proteins are protected from MNase digestion.

These data suggest that the initial site of nuclease cleavage in chromatin resides within the DNA bridging the repeating monomeric subunits. Further attack results in cleavage at a set of sites within the monomer liberating a pattern of smaller DNA fragments which probably represents the points of intimate contact between the histones and DNA.
evidence.rationale: Supports preferential linker cleavage and explains why retention is conditional on digestion rather than absolute protection of every nucleosome.

operations.label: MNase digestion
operations.description: Micrococcal nuclease acts on chromatin-associated genomic DNA. Preferential cleavage of exposed/linker DNA generates a digest from which trimmed, protected DNA-protein particles can be retained.
operations.mechanism: Nuclease cleavage changes the DNA fragment boundaries while protein association confers relative protection. MNase is the enzyme reagent; the orange circles are interpreted as generic activity symbols rather than consumed substrate or product.
operations.information_effect: Converts differences in DNA protection into differential survival and fragment boundaries in the DNA. Protection is preferential and digestion-dependent, not perfect nucleosome specificity.

operations.label: DNA extraction
operations.description: Recover the protected DNA from the isolated DNA-protein particles, changing the retained material from protein-associated fragments to free DNA.
operations.information_effect: DNA sequence retains the association with the genomic region that survived digestion; the protecting protein is removed from the readout carrier.
